Malimono, Sungao del Norte Ladles/Gentiemen: This refers to your earlier individual letters, which we deemed proper to consolidate considering that they all pertain to one subject matter, that is, on whether or not you can use u-je funds allocated to your respective municipalities by Congressman Francisco T. Matugas, out of the latter's Priority Development Fund (PDAF), as intelligence fund to bolster the peace and order campaign in your respective localities. Per your letters, the allocation was paruculariy requested tor the aforementioned purpose in direct response to the operations of the New People's Army (NPA) in your respective localities which danger still looms up to present. Before we answer your quenes, may we respectfully inform you, at the outset, that if peace and order is a priority investment area in a local government unit, an allocation for peace and order concems maybe provided in your annual budget. Funds for Intelligence or Confidential Purposes may be sourced from a certain percentage of the: (a) appropriations for peace and order; or (b) total

annual appropnabons whichever IS lower. (DILG Memorandum Circular No. 99- 65, dated 23 April 1999, Items 11.1 and 11.2). In your cases, Congressman Matugas has allocated funas in your respective municipalities out of his PDAF which you, in turn, intend to use as intelligence or anti-insurgency funds. Coming now to your queries, please be that we already answered a similar query in the past. Attached is a copy of our most recent opinion, DILG Opinion No. 68 s. 2009, dated 11 December 2009, for your ready reference. In said legal opinion, we found no legal impediment to such proposal. Such allocation to your respective municipalities from Congressman Matugas' PDAF may be considered as a "trust fund" which is allowed under the law. Congressman Matugas may be considered as a "trustor" who conveyed a part of his PDAF to you, as 'fruÄees" being the local chief executives of your respective municipalities, who will hold and administer such funds to finance the activities to be done in furtherance to the purpose upon which the said trust fund was cæated subject to the usual auditing and accounöng rules.
